captions.caption: A close-up view shows young green corn plants emerging from dry soil in a field.
Rows of small corn seedlings are visible, with some plants appearing damaged or missing.
The camera focuses on a specific corn plant that has been severed at the base.
A damaged corn seedling lies flat on the ground, likely due to cutworm activity.
The scene shifts to show a wide perspective of the cornfield under a bright, sunny sky.
A man in a checkered shirt and jeans is seen kneeling in the middle of the field.
The man begins to explain the impact of cutworms on young corn plants while gesturing.
He points to the soil near a corn plant, describing how pests attack at night.
The man continues his explanation, using his hands to illustrate the damage caused by insects.
He looks at the camera and notes that small plants can sometimes regrow after damage.
The man uses a small hand trowel to indicate a specific spot in the dirt.
He discusses the difference between cutworm damage and wireworm damage in corn crops.
The man leans forward to start investigating the soil for the presence of pests.
He uses his hand trowel to begin digging into the dry earth near a seedling.
The man continues to dig carefully, explaining the process of scouting for soil-dwelling insects.
He moves the soil around with his trowel, searching for signs of wireworms.
The man explains that digging is necessary to find certain types of pests in the field.
He continues to dig a small hole, focused on finding the cause of the crop damage.
The man mentions that cutworms can also be found by digging, though it's sometimes difficult.
He pauses to look at the camera while continuing his explanation about field scouting.
The man resumes digging, using the trowel to shift more soil out of the way.
He explains that larger pests are typically easier to locate during a field inspection.
The man uses his fingers to sift through some of the loose dirt he has unearthed.
He continues to speak to the camera, sharing his expertise on identifying crop pests.
The man uses the hand trowel to dig deeper into the soil in the same spot.
He carefully moves more dirt aside, maintaining a steady search for insects.
The man looks into the hole he is digging, explaining what he is looking for.
He continues to dig, his movements purposeful as he searches the soil.
The man explains that they are trying to determine why the corn is not growing there.
He uses the trowel to dig further, looking for the original seed or insect damage.
The man continues his explanation, noting that multiple factors can affect plant emergence.
He looks into the small excavation he has made in the agricultural field.
The man mentions that sometimes the issue is related to the planter rather than insects.
He continues to dig, emphasizing the importance of finding the corn seed.
The man uses the trowel to probe the soil, searching for evidence of pest damage.
He explains that identifying the specific insect is key to solving the problem.
The man continues to dig and sift through the dry soil with his trowel.
He looks closely at the ground, pointing out details to the camera.
The man explains the importance of scouting to manage corn pests effectively.
He continues to move dirt with the hand trowel, searching for any hidden larvae.
The man looks at the camera while kneeling, continuing his informative talk.
He uses the trowel to dig a bit more, carefully examining the unearthed soil.
The man pauses and looks at the area he has just scouted for insects.
He continues his explanation about the process of documenting field pests.
The man uses the trowel to sift through the dirt one last time.
He explains that once a pest is found, it's helpful to take a picture of it.
The man gestures with his hands while describing how to document pest findings.
He continues to speak to the camera, emphasizing the value of field data.
The man explains that having this information helps farmers make better decisions.
He looks at the camera while kneeling next to the small hole in the field.
The man continues his explanation, gesturing with his hands for emphasis.
He points towards the field, discussing the overall scouting process for corn.
The man looks back down at the soil, holding the trowel in his hand.
A graphic of a smartphone appears on the screen, promoting the RealAg mobile app.
The man continues to talk while the smartphone graphic is displayed.
He gestures with his hand as the on-screen text encourages downloading the app.
The man looks at the camera, explaining the benefits of using the app for scouting.
He continues his closing remarks while the app advertisement remains on screen.
The man gestures with both hands, concluding his presentation on field scouting.
The video ends with the man still kneeling in the cornfield as he finishes speaking.
